reasoning: IEA projects global solar PV generation overtakes wind by ~2026-2027 and hydropower by ~2029-2030, so within the 2023-2030 window solar plausibly becomes the largest single renewable. The drag is the Energy Institute Statistical Review's primary-energy substitution accounting (which inflates hydro) plus 2030 data needing to be published, but the trajectory clearly points to a qualifying year.

A reported, globally-scaled, satellite-facilitated wildlife-trade enforcement system producing a measurable >=5% poaching reduction with identifiable attribution and strict onus is not on track to exist by 2031. Pilots exist but no broad effective global system.

The 48-hour Atlantic track error was a record-low 45.4 nm in 2024 and ~53.4 nm in 2025; reaching 30.0 nm or less by 2030 would require an unprecedented ~35% further improvement in a few years, far outside the historical trend.

Satellite/AIS monitoring (e.g., Global Fishing Watch, SkyLight) is increasingly used in IUU enforcement, but a credible, broadly-applicable, attributable >=5% reduction in illegal fishing meeting the strict onus and 'directly implemented in enforcement' bar is unlikely to be cleanly reported by 2031.

The High Seas Treaty (BBNJ) has not yet entered into force and lacks operational enforcement machinery; demonstrable satellite-enabled enforcement outcomes specifically attributable to the treaty before Jan 2027 are very improbable.

Space-based solar power remains experimental with no commercial Earth-delivery capacity; it has essentially zero chance of exceeding total earth-based renewable capacity in any year through 2073, despite the long window.

Missions like MethaneSAT, CO2M (Copernicus, ~2026+), GOSAT-GW and Carbon Mapper are rapidly improving near-real-time GHG monitoring, but accurate (+/-5%) global real-time coverage of all CO2 and CH4 sources confirmed by multiple credible bodies likely takes into the early-to-mid 2030s, with a long tail.

The satellite-specific hyperspectral imagery segment is a niche slice of the broad hyperspectral imaging systems market (whose 2030 estimates range ~$1.8B-$28B across medical, industrial and ground uses). Satellite hyperspectral imagery revenue in 2030 most plausibly sits in the high-hundreds-of-millions to low-billions, centered near ~$1.1B.
